One person was killed and at least three others were injured in a shooting that happened at a New Jersey vigil, according to a report.

Mourners in Elizabeth had gathered to remember a man who was killed around seven years ago when shots rang out at around 8:30 p.m. Monday, CBS New York reported.

“A lot of shots were fired,” a witness told WABC.

One so-far unidentified person was pronounced dead at the scene, while three others were injured, according to the report, citing officials.

Two people were shot in the arms and legs, while one was shot in the chest. They were rushed to University Hospital in Newark. Their conditions are currently unknown.

Investigators are also probing a red car that fled the scene and was found burned out around four miles away.

They are investigating whether the car is linked to the shooting.

No arrests have been made, according to reports.
news.content: پوشش بیشتر ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. طبق یک گزارش، در تیراندازی که در نیوجرسی رخ داد، یک نفر کشته و حداقل سه نفر زخمی شدند. عزاداران در الیزابت گرد هم آمده بودند تا مردی را به یاد بیاورند که حدود هفت سال پیش با صدای شلیک گلوله ها در حدود ساعت 8:30 بعد از ظهر کشته شد. روز دوشنبه، CBS نیویورک گزارش داد. یکی از شاهدان به WABC گفت: "تیراندازی های زیادی شلیک شد." بر اساس این گزارش به نقل از مقامات، یک فرد ناشناس در محل کشته شده و سه نفر دیگر مجروح شده اند. دو نفر از ناحیه دست و پا مورد اصابت گلوله قرار گرفتند و یک نفر نیز از ناحیه سینه مورد اصابت گلوله قرار گرفت. آنها به سرعت به بیمارستان دانشگاه در نیوآرک منتقل شدند. وضعیت آنها در حال حاضر نامعلوم است. بازرسان همچنین در حال بررسی یک خودروی قرمز رنگ هستند که از محل متواری شده و در حدود چهار مایلی دورتر سوخته شده است. آنها در حال بررسی این هستند که آیا خودرو با تیراندازی مرتبط است یا خیر. بنا بر گزارش ها، هیچ بازداشتی صورت نگرفته است.

Just one child doomed China’s hopes of overtaking the US.

The Middle Kingdom, once a surging economic growth engine expected to eclipse the US economy in just a few years, is not expected to outgrow the US until the 2040s now — if it does at all.

And it’s largely down to China’s 1979 One Child Policy, which is devastating growth, according to Yi Fuxian, a Chinese demographer at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Plummeting birth rates and economic problems have erased the 6+% per year growth that China reported before the COVID-19 pandemic.

Many economists in both China and the West were taken in by the Chinese Communist Party’s inflated official figures, which massively overestimated the country’s consumer power, Fuxian said.

It comes as a Goldman Sachs study found that China’s population began shrinking in 2022, just 13 years after that of neighboring Japan. And its decline is on track to be far steeper, dramatically damaging the country’s economic prospects, the Financial Times reported.

China has a GDP of $21.6 trillion — just two-thirds the size of the US economy.

Yi told The Post that official Chinese statistics have systematically inflated the country’s birthrates and total population figures going back decades.

While official reports claim China has a population of over 1.4 billion, Yi calculates that the true figure in 2020 was “under 1.28 billion,” at least 130 million lower than reported.

India actually surpassed China as the world’s most populous nation years earlier than officially recognized, according to Yi, author of the 2007 book, “Big Country with an Empty Nest,” which criticized China’s one-child policies.

The US, the third most populous country in the world, has 342 million people — about a quarter the population of China.

Yi argues that China’s population actually began shrinking in 2018, four years earlier than Goldman Sachs’ estimate, and more than a decade before the official projection of 2031 to 2034.

Most of this can be attributed to China’s notorious One Child Policy, instituted to limit Chinese families to one child per mother, over fears of spiraling population growth and widespread poverty.

While the policy was relaxed to two children per couple in 2016 and three children in 2021, China’s total fertility rate remains one of the lowest in the world.

China is no longer poor — officially 0% of the population is in extreme poverty, compared to 88% 40 years ago.

But it’s also not rich; the per capita GDP is about $13,800 per year, about 15% of that in the US.

Turkey, Russia and Kazakhstan are all richer than China by that measure.

The country’s total fertility rate fell below the 2.1 replacement level in 1991 and continued to plummet, dropping below 1.0 and now estimated to be just 0.8 births per woman, according to Yi.

Last year saw a record low of just 8 million live births in China. The much smaller US, by contrast, had 3.6 million births.

Yi also blames the economic reforms of China’s former Premier Zhu Rongji in the 1990s, for causing “many problems” that slowed down China’s economic growth and race to catch up with the US.

Decades of strict birth restrictions and fiscal centralization severely curtailed household disposable income in China, to roughly 42-44% of GDP.

In contrast, in the US, that figure is over 70% of GDP.

While this may have helped China’s economy in the short term, allowing it to flood the US with cheap imported goods, in the long run, it may have signed the CCP’s suicide note, according to Yi.

Children function as “super-consumers,” driving much of household spending, he explained.

With China missing several full generations worth of children, this severely crippled Chinese domestic consumption, he argued.

To offset weak domestic consumption, China became heavily dependent on manufacturing exports, an unsustainable real estate bubble, and state-subsidized industrial overcapacity, he explained.

Those policies, “killed China’s economy, the population and the economy — and also killed America’s manufacturing,” Yi said.

China is now one of the oldest countries in the world, with a rapidly shrinking labor pool and aging population. The median age is expected to reach 59 by 2050, compared to 44 in the US.

This means Beijing may never catch up with the US economically — and worse, could face a long-term economic deceleration, Yi argued.

Yi puts the over-optimistic predictions about China’s economic growth down to mainstream economists and Chinese government-aligned institutions relying on fabricated data — assuming China’s population would soon grow five times larger than the US.

This played into the popular narrative that “the East is rising while the West is declining,” he said, while the truth is very different.

“By 2029 to 2035, China will lag behind the US across all major demographic and growth metrics,” Yi said.

However, for pro-democracy activists who might hope that this demographic time bomb could topple the CCP, Yi has a warning.

Contrary to Western expectations that economic development would foster a pro-democracy middle class, China’s rapid aging has depleted it of the young population required to drive political activism.

Just 16% of China is aged 15 to 29, down from 31% at the time of China’s last mass-democracy movement in 1989, which culminated in the communists’ brutal crackdown in Tiananmen Square.

An aging, risk-averse China is far more likely to support a centralized strongman who will safeguard pensions and social stability, Yi explained.
news.content: پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود بیشتر مشاهده کنید. فقط یک کودک امیدهای چین برای سبقت گرفتن از ایالات متحده را محکوم کرد. پادشاهی میانه که زمانی موتور رشد اقتصادی فزاینده ای بود که انتظار می رفت اقتصاد ایالات متحده را ظرف چند سال تحت الشعاع قرار دهد، اکنون انتظار نمی رود تا دهه 2040 از ایالات متحده پیشی بگیرد - اگر اصلاً چنین کند. به گفته یی فوکسیان، جمعیت شناس چینی در دانشگاه ویسکانسین-مدیسون، این تا حد زیادی به سیاست یک فرزند چین در سال 1979 مربوط می شود که رشد ویرانگر است. کاهش نرخ زاد و ولد و مشکلات اقتصادی رشد 6+ درصدی در سال را که چین قبل از همه گیری کووید-19 گزارش می کرد، از بین برده است. فوکسیان گفت که بسیاری از اقتصاددانان در چین و غرب با ارقام رسمی متورم حزب کمونیست چین که به شدت قدرت مصرف این کشور را بیش از حد تخمین می‌زند مورد توجه قرار گرفتند. این درحالی است که مطالعه گلدمن ساکس نشان می‌دهد که جمعیت چین در سال 2022، تنها 13 سال پس از جمعیت همسایه ژاپن، شروع به کاهش کرد. فایننشال تایمز گزارش داد که کاهش آن در مسیری بسیار تندتر است و به چشم‌انداز اقتصادی کشور آسیب می‌زند. چین دارای تولید ناخالص داخلی 21.6 تریلیون دلاری است - فقط دو سوم اندازه اقتصاد ایالات متحده. با 4 میلیارد، یی محاسبه می کند که رقم واقعی در سال 2020 "زیر 1.28 میلیارد" بوده است، حداقل 130 میلیون کمتر از آنچه گزارش شده است. هند در واقع

Few words can stop a new parent’s heart quite like “NICU.”

Nearly 1 in 10 US babies are whisked to the neonatal intensive care unit at birth, often because they are preterm or critically ill. It can be a really scary place to start life.

My premature twins, born at 33 weeks and four days, spent several weeks in the NICU tethered to machines that helped them breathe and consume breast milk.

Before they could get discharged, they had to breathe and feed independently and pass a 90-minute car seat test.

Every hospital requires babies to go home in a car seat to comply with state safety laws.

NICU babies, for their part, tend to have underdeveloped neck and chest muscles that cause them to slump in a car seat, leading to breathing difficulties or drops in their heart rate and oxygen.

In the test, nurses track an infant’s heart rate, breathing rate and oxygen levels in the car seat to make sure it’s safe for them to travel home.

One of my twins failed the car seat test twice because her oxygen dropped too low. She passed the third time, but we were concerned about bringing her home without the machines that had monitored her vitals since birth.

Our NICU doctor suggested we try an Owlet Baby Monitor. It’s designed to track an infant’s pulse rate, oxygen and sleep trends and alert parents in real time if something is wrong.

Her recommendation did come with a warning: The Owlet could cause false alarms, needlessly sending us to the emergency room.

Unfortunately, the hospital did not allow us to put the FDA-cleared Dream Sock ($299) on our baby while she was hooked up to the machines to test its accuracy.

We were on our own with the sock, which looks like a tiny gladiator sandal and fits snugly on a baby’s foot thanks to Velcro-like straps.

It contains an electronic sensor that feeds info to the Owlet Dream app on the parent’s phone.

Some of the data was insight we hadn’t received in the hospital, like whether our daughter was sleeping lightly or deeply.

We were alerted a few times when her oxygen started to slip during mealtime, and we changed her feeding position accordingly. Fair warning: The siren is LOUD. You do not forget your first Owlet alarm, which is helpful for acting fast.

One major downside is that the device will blare if the baby has kicked it off or if it has been carried out of range of its base reader.

Being kicked loose doesn’t trigger the same alarm as a critical breathing event — as in, the baby is not breathing — but prepare to be startled at least once for a harmless reason.

I jolted my husband awake a few times when I brought the baby outside to let our dog out, and the Owlet bleated because it was out of range.

As a new parent, especially one who has spent time in the NICU, the last thing you need is another headache.

Furthermore, our pediatrician warned that new parents can become fixated on the app and overreact to the slightest change in the baby’s stats.

However, I’m glad we tried the Owlet. We used the device until our twin posted good numbers over several weeks.

It could prove useful for babies like ours with a history of respiratory issues or those struggling to find their bedtime groove. The Owlet takes the guesswork out of a lot of aspects of newborn life.

تقریباً از هر 10 نوزاد ایالات متحده، 1 نفر در هنگام تولد به بخش مراقبت های ویژه نوزادان منتقل می شود، اغلب به این دلیل که زودرس یا بدخیم هستند. این می تواند مکانی واقعاً ترسناک برای شروع زندگی باشد. دوقلوهای نارس من که در 33 هفته و چهار روز به دنیا آمدند، چندین هفته را در NICU گذراندند و به دستگاه هایی متصل شدند که به آنها کمک می کرد نفس بکشند و شیر مادر را مصرف کنند. قبل از اینکه بتوانند مرخص شوند، باید به طور مستقل نفس می‌کشیدند و تغذیه می‌کردند و آزمایش 90 دقیقه‌ای صندلی ماشین را پشت سر می‌گذاشتند. هر بیمارستانی از نوزادان می‌خواهد که با صندلی ماشین به خانه بروند تا قوانین ایمنی دولتی را رعایت کنند. نوزادان NICU، به نوبه خود، معمولاً عضلات گردن و قفسه سینه‌شان توسعه نیافته است که باعث می‌شود در صندلی ماشین بیفتند یا ضربان قلبشان به مشکل بخورد. در این آزمایش، پرستاران ضربان قلب، ضربان تنفس و سطح اکسیژن نوزاد را در صندلی ماشین ردیابی می‌کنند تا مطمئن شوند که سفر به خانه برای آن‌ها ایمن است. یکی از دوقلوهای من دو بار در تست صندلی ماشین مردود شد زیرا اکسیژن او خیلی کم شده بود. او بار سوم را پشت سر گذاشت، اما ما نگران بودیم که او را بدون دستگاه‌هایی که از بدو تولد وضعیت حیاتی او را کنترل می‌کردند به خانه بیاوریم. پزشک NICU ما پیشنهاد داد که یک مانیتور کودک Owlet را امتحان کنیم. این برای ردیابی ضربان نبض، روند اکسیژن و خواب نوزاد طراحی شده است و در صورت بروز مشکل به والدین در زمان واقعی هشدار می دهد. توصیه او همراه با یک اخطار بود: جغد می تواند هشدارهای کاذب ایجاد کند و بیهوده برای ما ارسال کند.

When Adam Fox inked his extension with the Rangers five years ago Sunday, it reset the market for defensemen coming off their entry-level deals and instantly placed him in the upper tier of blue-line contracts around the league. He landed a seven-year, $66.5 million deal — a $9.5 million rate in average annual value — months after completing his Norris Trophy-winning season in 2020-21 and has lived up to the point-per-game expectations since.

Get Mollie Walker’s text messages with the latest Rangers buzz and get your questions answered — exclusive to Sports+ subscribers.

But over time, as the market for blueliners has continued to get reset with massive deal after massive deal, Fox’s annual price for the Blueshirts has quickly turned into a fleeting bargain. Avalanche star Cale Makar inked a $163.2 million extension over the summer, marking the first time in NHL history that a player topped $20 million in average annual value. Defenseman Quinn Hughes, an unrestricted free agent after the season, will likely surpass that threshold, too, regardless of whether his contract arrives via a Wild extension or with another team.

Fox, according to the CBA, will be extension-eligible once the 2027-28 season ends and the final year of his deal begins. He’ll only be 30 years old at that point, too, and 31 when his current contract ends. It is then that the Rangers will be forced to adjust to the rest of the market, where rising salary caps and massive deals will continue to reshape what the ultimate price tag will be for Fox’s next deal.

But it’s a topic worth revisiting this week given the anniversary of Fox’s extension with the team he grew up rooting for, the milestone of his 500th career game Monday night against the Kings and his tear of assists to open the season. Fox collected 16 assists through the Rangers’ first 13 games, leading all defensemen and sitting behind only Connor McDavid’s 25 for the NHL lead. His point total ranks 12th in the NHL, too, and leads all Rangers. It’s a 103-point pace, which would shatter Fox’s previous career-best of 74 in the 2021-22 campaign that also featured the extension.

President Trump blasted senators for not passing a bill that would make daylight saving time permanent – joking that the exercise of changing the clocks makes him late.

The commander-in-chief told supporters in Corinth, Mississippi, on Monday that the twice-yearly ritual is “stupid” and claimed “many many Americans are very disappointed” by stalling politicians.

“The House has already passed a bill five times to make daylight saving permanent. The Senate needs to take a vote,” Trump railed before recalling the moment he was late for a meeting.

“I’m always late. I had a big meeting and I was an hour late.”

Trump then claimed “everyone hates” the ritual and called on the Senate to “vote [clock-changing] out” and “go back to one time.”

“No more changing the clock,” he said.

Trump claimed the Sunshine Protection Act “remains locked” in the Senate – even though it was passed by the House on a 308-117 margin.

“Daylight saving time will end as scheduled to the disappointment of many, many Americans,” Trump lamented.

Trump is a prominent critic of clock-changing and on Sunday blasted the Senate  for “letting the Daylight Saving Bill die.”

He has previously accused Arkansas Senator Tom Cotton of holding up the bill – ramping up pressure on lawmakers to pass it.

Daylight saving time will end on the morning of Nov. 1 – much to the frustration of the president.

Permanent daylight saving time would mean more sun in the afternoon and evening hours.

But despite the president’s pressure, Cotton (R-Ark.) is not relenting – having vowed to “always oppose” the reform.

“For many Arkansans, permanent Daylight Savings Time would mean the sun wouldn’t rise until after 8:00 or even 8:30 a.m. during the dead of winter. Three months out of the year, kids in towns like Bentonville, Fayetteville, and Fort Smith would start school ahead of the sun,” Cotton said.

“Meanwhile, construction workers, farmers, and others who rise before the sun or need the sun to work would be penalized.

“These workers might go three, four, even five hours in the morning without seeing the sun, which would hurt their quality of life and potentially their safety in the workplace.”

Cotton allowed that “clock changes can be bad for health, but the best evidence suggests that the natural rhythms of our internal body clocks align more closely with Standard Time than Daylight Savings Time.”

Senator Steve Daines (R-Mont.) has also warned that lawmakers in the western US could push back.

“I can see where Florida likes it for tee times at certain times of the year, but it doesn’t work so well for moms and dads putting kids on buses when the sunrise in Western Montana wouldn’t be until 9:30 in the morning. It’s not going to work for us,” he told CNN in July.

He joked the bill wouldn’t “see the light of day.”

پوشش بیشتر ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. رئیس جمهور ترامپ سناتورها را به دلیل تصویب نکردن لایحه ای که باعث دائمی شدن ساعت تابستانی می شود مورد انتقاد قرار داد - به شوخی گفت که تغییر ساعت باعث تأخیر او می شود. فرمانده کل قوا روز دوشنبه به حامیان خود در کورینث، می سی سی پی گفت که این مراسم دو بار سالانه بسیار "احمقانه" است و بسیاری از آمریکایی ها ادعا می کنند که "احمقانه" هستند. ترامپ پیش از یادآوری لحظه تأخیر خود در جلسه، گفت: «مجلس تا کنون پنج بار لایحه‌ای را تصویب کرده است تا صرفه‌جویی در روز را دائمی کند. سنا باید رأی‌گیری کند.» «من همیشه دیر می‌آیم. یک جلسه بزرگ داشتم و یک ساعت تأخیر داشتم.»
ترامپ سپس مدعی شد که «همه از این مراسم متنفرند» و از سنا خواست که «رای دهند [تغییر ساعت]» و «به یک زمان برگردند».
او گفت: «دیگر ساعت را عوض نمی‌کنیم. ترامپ مدعی شد که قانون حفاظت از آفتاب در سنا «قفل مانده است» - حتی اگر مجلس با اختلاف 308-117 به تصویب رسید. ترامپ اظهار تاسف کرد: «ساعت تابستانی طبق برنامه‌ریزی‌شده برای ناامیدی بسیاری از آمریکایی‌ها به پایان می‌رسد. ترامپ منتقد برجسته تغییر ساعت است و در روز یکشنبه «تغییر ساعت» را برای روز یکشنبه به پایان می‌رساند. او قبلاً سناتور آرکانزاس تام کاتن را متهم کرده بود که این لایحه را به تعویق انداخته است - فشار بر قانونگذاران برای تصویب آن را تشدید می کند. ساعت تابستانی در صبح روز اول نوامبر به پایان می رسد - که باعث ناامیدی رئیس جمهور می شود.

news.originalContent:
The cars have gone, and so have the buses, but while retailers expect a boost, residents worry about change.

London, United Kingdom – “It’s magical,” says biology teacher Muneera Alfadhel from under her umbrella.

In fact, it is a characteristically rainy, grey day in London, but the weather is doing nothing to dampen her mood. She is among the first to walk down the middle of the iconic Oxford Street following its pedestrianisation.

For generations, shoppers have bustled along Oxford Street next to bikes, cars, black cabs and red double-decker buses. But on Monday, from Great Portland Street to Orchard Street, the road is now a pedestrian-only zone.

On Monday morning, by force of habit, most pedestrians are still sticking to the pavement. Mark Arbouine, a forensic scientist out for a stroll, is one of the few breaking ranks: “I saw there was no traffic today, so I thought, why not walk in the middle of the street and take advantage of it? I just think it’s great for the environment, great for shopping. It’s just so much easier to move around the street.”

This tiny strip of real estate is big business: about 1 percent of the UK’s annual gross domestic product (GDP) is generated along this 1km (0.6 miles) stretch of street. But despite its outsized importance, Oxford Street has in recent decades been hit by lower consumer spending, as well as falling rents and footfall, which is now just 57 percent of what it was in 2006, according to New West End Company, a retail trade body.

The Greater London Authority, also known as City Hall, believes pedestrianisation could, therefore, offer a lifeline.

City Hall analysis suggests the partial pedestrianisation of Oxford Street could generate more than $109m per year and support an additional 700 jobs. Following a weekend trial in October 2025, two-thirds of businesses in the area said they had higher or similar sales figures during the pedestrianisation.

This is the first step in a multi-phase regeneration project to add two public squares, 50 trees and hundreds of public seating.

Barbara Stoll, a leading campaigner on the benefits of greener, more walkable cities, was smiling as she observed the street. The air already feels cleaner, she noted.

“It’s amazing coming here this morning. Walking down the street, it was already so uplifting that the noise is considerably lower,” she said. “People are excited. I saw people coming up from the tube and looking around. Seeing that, it’s almost like children when it’s Christmas Day.

“So I think it’s absolutely wonderful, and so needed for London.”

On Saturday, ahead of the change, not all shoppers were convinced. A French tourist said he would avoid Oxford Street altogether if buses and cabs were no longer allowed through.

“People with disabilities who cannot walk a lot – that would be really helpful if the buses move on and they don’t discontinue [them],” a shopper told Al Jazeera.

“It would be good. Sometimes you’re tired; sometimes it’s raining.”

The pedestrianisation of Oxford Street has been years in the making, and not without controversy.

London Mayor Sadiq Khan first tried it in 2017, following a manifesto pledge. But the plan fell apart in 2018, when Westminster Council – the local government authority responsible for Oxford Street at the time – withdrew its backing, saying residents did not support it.

Following a public consultation, Khan created the Oxford Street Development Corporation, taking responsibility for the street away from local officials and transferring it to the Greater London Authority and Transport for London.

With this second, successful attempt at pedestrianisation, doubts from local authorities have not gone away.

Residents are not being listened to, said Councillor Tim Barnes, the deputy leader and cabinet member for growth and planning for the City of Westminster.

“There has been a communication process with residents, but it’s been pretty much one way. Mostly, they are being told what’s going to happen to them and how it’s going to happen; what the format of the process is going to be in future. But realistically, those who know the street best haven’t really been listened to.”

He believes the economic benefits are overstated and do not consider the impact of displacing bus routes from a major road to the surrounding, smaller streets. That fear is shared by resident Nerma Cridge, who said London’s West End will become “completely unliveable, too crowded and too noisy at night”.

“We think all of this should be done in a much more productive relationship with communities,” she told Al Jazeera over the phone.

Concerns over the change will fade once residents see the real-world results in the coming months, Stoll believes.

“Examples from across Europe and the world, where such projects have already happened, prove that this only makes life better overall for local residents,” she said.

“Retail gets a boost. More people linger, more people come to the street, more people spend money in the shops, and even local shop vacancies reduce. The local air pollution significantly reduces, and as activity increases, people just take back the space.”

The Oxford Street Development Corporation will be testing and reviewing the results of the pedestrianisation in the coming months, and reviewing its findings early next year. Transitioning the rest of Oxford Street into a permanent, traffic-free public space is expected to go ahead by the end of next year.

Ahead of mayoral elections in 2028, the pedestrianisation could be one of the last major initiatives that Sadiq Khan signs off. A landmark project that will also become his legacy.

Rachel is a 41-year-old doctor in Bergen County, New Jersey. She has a solid, loving marriage to a fellow MD, two boisterous kids under seven, and one method that she uses to stay sane:

Specifically, the kind of highbrow erotica with the same explicit content as a softcore video, but made by award-winning filmmakers and novelists, and starring Oscar-winning actors instead of OnlyFans girls.

“It’s become like my therapy,” said the family medicine specialist, who plays XXX-rated audiobooks like “Helpless” by Jessica Knoll and “A Court of Thorns and Roses” by Sarah J. Maas when she’s driving alone in her family SUV, and watches movies like “Baby Girl” and shows like “Industry” on her iPhone while doing laundry.

In another generation, Rachel would likely need to keep her sex-positive programming under wraps. Not today.

“My group chat is full of moms who trade [sex content] recommendations,” Rachel told The Post. “It feels like you’re watching any other good movie… just with bondage.”

Rachel and her friends are reaping the rewards of prestige porn, a new genre where 40+ women are centered in highbrow erotica about sexual dominance and desire — in movies, in books and at upscale fashion and beauty boutiques.

Think “Fifty Shades” for women who have a mortgage, a career and no patience for fake bags… or fake orgasms.

The era of prestige porn means Oscar winners like Nicole Kidman, 59, and Olivia Colman, 52, can engage in once-unthinkable graphic acts for au courant movie studios like A24. Jessica Knoll, who has made millions writing crime thrillers, is now a Gen X Anais Nin writing about unspeakable — but delightfully readable — sex acts in her bestselling new book “Helpless.”

Meanwhile, Bloomingdale’s now sells $108 “arouse stimulating serum” alongside its Louis Vuitton purses; at Revolve, there are anal beads and Isabel Marant. And the $60 erotica app Quinn tells bedtime stories spicier than Blue Ribbon’s wasabi, read by Emmy nominee (and Dior darling) Andrew Scott.

The latest entry into these artful new films came this weekend: “Wicker,” an “absurdist romantic comedy” starring Colman as a frustrated spinster and Alexander Skarsgård as a man made of straw who gives her a roll in the hay.

When its steamy trailer debuted in July, it went so viral that doctors had to warn people against pleasuring themselves with “trees or shrubs.”

The movie opens nationwide on Oct. 30, but advance screenings for the show — including several with “vibrating and motion seats” — sold out across the country.

Reddit reports say the theaters are full of older women. In Florida’s Palm Beach Gardens, The Post saw an entire screening room full of female retirees.

“Very enjoyable,” said one 74-year-old woman named Joyce after the movie, under the condition that she withhold her last name. “My kids read your paper.”

Why is our era so ripe for prestige porn?

“People are totally disconnected from their bodies right now,” said Brianna Makówka, MSEd, LMHC, CST, a licensed sex therapist who specializes in kink therapy. She told The Post that between social media, dating apps and remote work, “we’re living in screens so often that our bodies are reminding us how important they are to our full being.”

Prestige porn, she argues, is letting us frame sex as not just desirable but luxurious, which gives people — especially women — permission to engage in it more openly.

“This new wave of luxury sex products and more artful erotic content is letting more people engage with sex, and pushing us to ask, ‘What is the type of sex worth having?’”

Putting kink in a luxury setting, she said, lets people explore sexual desire without stigma. “It’s giving a lot of people permission to get curious about asking, ‘What is it that I want from sex?’” she explained.

Theater director Rob Ashford thinks his new Off-Broadway show, “Memoirs of Amorous Gentlemen,” is a hit because it depicts themes like sexual role play and bondage with “curiosity instead of judgement” — and with an eye toward the eerier effects of Ozempic

“We’re so obsessed with body control and weight. We have GLP1s. We have a doctor that can make anything bigger or smaller. But the corsets in our show, they give our characters this instant gratification, no shot, no scalpel. There’s a pleasure in that, especially for Gen X women who have been told their whole lives that their bodies are not enough.”

NYC designer Jennifer Zuccarini runs the upscale lingerie brand Fleur du Mal, which has designed peek-a-boo pieces for Taylor Swift and Zendaya. (She is also the creator of the viral $128 Knicks All-Star bra in blue satin and orange lace.)

Zuccarini says her three New York boutiques — in Nolita, the Upper East Side, and Williamsburg — are routinely “crowded” with older women coming directly from luxury stores like Chanel and Dior who are seeking “the same type of designer experience in the bedroom.”

“Sex is such a luxury right now because we’re on devices constantly,” she told The Post. “We’re disconnected. We say ‘touch grass’ but there’s also touching someone else. When you have that feeling with somebody, there’s no better drug out there.”

Zuccarini said it’s common for shoppers to visit her store asking for a simple bra or lace panty, but leave with a pair of $300 leather handcuffs. “Luxury helps legitimize sexual taste and preferences,” she explained.

Prestige porn even comes with its own luxury lube, as created by Éva Goicochea for her sexual wellness line Maude. Goicochea thinks that sex is “the final frontier” for adult women who have already conquered the boardroom, built dream wardrobes, and often had families — but not with total satisfaction in bed.

“Elevated design gives people permission to view sex as something they should feel good about wanting and exploring,” said Goicochea, who counts the Hollywood bombshell Dakota Johnson as a business partner.

Maude was one of Sephora’s first-ever sexual wellness brands; today it sells lube and vibrators at Ulta Beauty next to Naomi Watt’s sexual wellness line, Stripes, which was created especially for post-menopausal libidos.

Gwyneth Paltrow, 54, sells her own lubrication — called “Sex Oil” — through her Goop wellness empire for $55.

“Buying an intimate oil or a sex toy should be as mundane and shame-free as buying a face cream,” Goop’s editorial director, Kylie Gilbert, told The Post, adding that frank chats on sexual pleasure have been part of “Gwyneth’s vision of Goop from day one.” She notes that the Goop lube is a longtime bestseller.

Perhaps the big hook for prestige porn is that it refuses to call itself porn at all. In press interviews for “Wicker,” both Colman and Skarsgård are careful to call the movie a “romance” despite its explicit content.

“Industry” is described by HBO as a “gripping and provocative” drama despite its penchant for strap-ons and fellatio scenes. And the Nicole Kidman hit “Babygirl” features the Oscar winner on all fours, pretending to be a dog, licking candy out of her 20-something intern’s hand before getting thrashed in bed.

Makówka, the sex therapist,  says all this is pretty great.

“A lot of people might have a curiosity of a power exchange dynamic —a dominant and submissive relationship that’s about leadership and surrender,” she said.

“Films like these are giving a lot of people permission to get curious about asking, ‘What is it that I want? What have I not been seeking? Maybe it’s okay to seek this out.’ That is healthier, psychologically, for everyone. It makes people happier and more connected.”

Tech devices don’t do that, says Makówka.

New Yorkers dreaming of trading their rental keys for a home of their own are facing a brutal reality — one in which they’re squeezed on both sides.

Buying a typical home in the Big Apple now costs nearly $7,000 more per month than renting, thanks to languishing high mortgage rates — making saving for that dream purchase impossible these days as rents hit yet another record high.

The monthly cost of purchasing a median-priced home in New York City reached a hefty $10,737 in the third quarter of 2026 — a whopping $6,952, or 184%, more than the city’s median asking rent of $3,785, according to a new Realtor.com report.

And while home prices have dipped slightly, it doesn’t make much of a difference.

The median listing price in the city fell 2% year-over-year to roughly $1.41 million, bringing the estimated monthly cost of ownership down about 1%, or $107, from a year earlier.

But mortgage rates climbed above 7% in late September, in the fourth quarter of the year. At that rate, the monthly cost of buying the same home would jump to approximately $11,008 — $164 more than a year ago.

The calculations assume a 10% down payment on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage and include estimated property taxes, homeowners insurance, and fees including common charges and maintenance.

Meanwhile, renting isn’t exactly getting cheaper either.

The city’s median asking rent hit a record $3,785 in the third quarter, up $162, or 4.5%, from a year earlier — its highest level since Realtor.com began tracking the data in 2019. That puts rents $816, or 27.5%, above pre-pandemic levels.

“NYC’s record-high rents in Q3 2026 are largely the result of sustained rental demand and a shortage of rental inventory,” Jiayi Xu, senior economist at Realtor.com, told The Post.

To make things even worse moving forward, a Mamdani campaign pledge that recently became official.

“Looking ahead, the rent freeze that took effect on Oct. 1 could add upward pressure on market rents. The freeze bars rent increases for one- and two-year lease renewals for roughly 1 million rent-stabilized apartments through Sept. 30, 2027.”

Asking rents for studios through two-bedroom units surged 7.1% year-over-year to $3,662, far outpacing the 2.9% increase for homes with three or more bedrooms, which now command a median $5,089.

The pain is particularly acute in Manhattan, where median asking rents soared 8.3% annually to $5,375 — the steepest increase among the four boroughs covered by the report.

Brooklyn followed with a 4.9% jump to $4,197, while Queens rents climbed 3.9% to $3,744. The Bronx remained the least expensive of the four, though rents there still rose 2.7% to $3,233. Staten Island was not included.

And the income needed to comfortably afford a New York apartment is eye-watering.

Under the widely used guideline that housing should consume no more than 30% of household income, Manhattan renters would need to earn $215,000 annually to afford the borough’s median asking rent.

That threshold drops to $167,880 in Brooklyn, $149,760 in Queens and $129,320 in The Bronx.

As The Post recently reported, even a six-figure salary doesn’t stretch particularly far in the New York area, where a $100,000 household income can afford a median of just 801 square feet and one bedroom — compared with a four-bedroom home in Memphis.

Making matters worse, paychecks aren’t keeping pace with housing costs for many New Yorkers.

Average hourly earnings among private-sector workers in the city increased 4.2% year-over-year in August, trailing the 4.5% overall rent increase and falling well short of the 7.1% jump for smaller rentals.

Workers in some industries fared even worse, with manufacturing wages rising just 1%, earnings in private education and health services remaining flat, and pay declining in construction and other goods-producing industries.

“New York City renters are facing a difficult affordability equation: rents are rising, especially for the smaller homes many renters compete for, while the cost of buying remains dramatically higher,” said Danielle Hale, chief economist at Realtor.com, in a statement.

“A modest decline in home prices brought some relief to the monthly cost of buying in the third quarter, but mortgage rates above 7% can quickly erase that progress. For renters hoping to save for a down payment, the squeeze is coming from both directions.”

Added Xu, “That combination makes it harder for renters to build savings and move toward homeownership.”

Toys “R” Us is scrambling to open 120 new stores by Thanksgiving — but suppliers burned by its devastating bankruptcy in 2017 remain skittish about doing business with the retailer’s new operators, The Post has learned.

Go Retail Group — a Texas-based business that specializes in pop-up stores, including two Disney Store Limited Time locations and Calendar.com shops — has has opened 40 year-round Toys “R” Us stores since 2024. It has opened the stores under license from WHP Global, a New York-based firm that owns 16 brands including Vera Wang, Marc Jacobs,  Anne Klein and Land’s End.

But as Go Retail looks to quadruple its number of Toys “R” Us locations in time for the crucial holiday season, it has been asking toy manufacturers for extended credit terms – asking to pay as much as 180 days after goods are delivered to its stores, multiple sources told The Post.

In response, many vendors have pushed back, with some noting that the industry norm for inventory financing is between 30 and 90 days.

“They should be the ones financing the business, not their vendors,” said Jay Foreman, chief executive of Basic Fun, maker of Tonka Trucks and Care Bears. “We went down that road once before and got badly burned and won’t put ourselves in that position again.”

Alan Dorfman of Super Impulse — which makes tiny, pocket-sized versions of toys and games including board games like Battleship, Connect 4 and Hungry Hungry Hippos — is also holding back.

“We hope to be part of it, but we are not yet shipping to them,” Dorfman told The Post. “We have worked with Go Retail in the past but there were some bumps in the road and we are trying to get things back on track.”

Founded 70 years ago by Charles Lazarus, the retailer operated more than 800 Toys “R” Us and Babies “R” Us stores in the US when it went belly up and liquidated in 2018. It was saddled with $5 billion in debt after being acquired by private equity giants Bain Capital, KKR and Vornado Realty Trust in 2005.

The implosion sparked millions of dollars in losses and years of chaos across the US toy supply chain. It also left longstanding bitterness among industry veterans.

Nevertheless, WHP Global has tapped Jamie Uitdenhowen, Toys “R” Us’s former vice president of merchandising, as executive vice president of the revived brand. Matthew Finigan, who had served as the company’s treasurer before the bankruptcy, is now the brand’s chief financial officer.

“There’s hesitation to do business with them because of the terms they are asking for,” said Michael Drake who headed up boys toys at Toys “R” Us headquarters in Paramus under Lazarus and says he has spoken with a dozen toymakers.

WHP acquired the brand in 2021 and launched partnerships with Macy’s and Go Retail among other smaller tie-ins. It has licensing partnerships abroad that operate some 1,680 stores in 37 countries.

“Like any retailer, we work to secure the best possible terms with our suppliers,” Go Retail CEO Gideon Schlessinger said in a statement. “We’ve been in the toy business for 26 years, managing significant seasonal inventory commitments and building longstanding vendor relationships. Our approach to purchasing and payment arrangements has been consistent throughout our history and remains unchanged today.”

In addition to Macy’s, there are some 40 Toys “R” Us stores opened in the US over the the past several years. A 20,000-square-foot flagship at American Dream mall in East Rutherford, NJ is run by a licensing partner called Parade Stores Inc., a Toys “R” Us spokesperson said.

Go Retail operates all of the other freestanding locations, including the additional 120 stores that are mostly opening in malls for about one year, a spokesperson for the company told The Post.

“We have not experienced any hesitation from suppliers about working with us under the Toys “R” Us brand,” Schlessinger said. “In fact, the strength and growth of Toys “R” Us have only enhanced those relationships.”

The store expansion comes as the $46 billion US toy industry is on an upswing with sales growing by 17% in the first half of the year — or the biggest such increase in six years, according to Circana. In its heyday, Toys “R” Us was the place where the industry launched new products, showcased the latest trends and allowed families to interact with the toys they might purchase.

Still, some question the retailer’s relevance today as rivals like Walmart, Target, Amazon and Five Below have expanded their toy offerings.

“It’s a tougher landscape for them to come back to,” said toy analyst Gerrick Johnson of Seaport Research. “Because others have stepped into the void they left.”

Before the bankruptcy, most Toys “R” Us stores were about 30,000 square feet, compared with the Go Retail stores that are between 3,500 to 7,000 square feet, say industry experts.

“The 120 mall pop ups won’t do the volume of even 20 Walmart stores,” predicted Foreman of Basic Fun.

Tom Neville, vice president of sales for Connetix, an Australian-based company that makes colorful, magnetic tiles, said he was surprised to learn from The Post that Toys “R” Us was already selling his company’s products online.

“They are definitely not buying directly from us,” Neville told The Post, adding that he guessed ToysRUs.com purchased Connetix from a distributor.

Neville said he had deliberately “stayed an arm’s length” from the toy departments at Macy’s that are branded Toys “R” Us, of which there more than 350, according to Macy’s.

“Most of the time you go into a Macy’s [toy department] and it’s sad,” Neville said. “It’s not merchandised well. The shelves are empty off season.”

Macy’s declined to comment on its toy offerings. The company has since closed dozens of stores since the partnership began in 2022.

Others are still on the fence about partnering with Toys “R” Us.

“I’ve been wondering whether the [new operators] are going to make this unique and bring in something new and different from what you can find on Amazon,” said Brian McDonald, vice president of sales and marketing for Ohio-based Simplay3, maker of outdoor activity sets and toys.

Simplay3 is open to working with Toys “R” Us, McDonald said, “but we got burned pretty good [by the bankruptcy], losing nearly $1 million and we would definitely be more cautious because of who they are.”

At the same time, “there’s also fear about missing out on an opportunity,” added Drake, the former Toys “R” Us executive.
news.content:
اطلاعات بیشتری از پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. Toys "R" Us در تلاش است تا 120 فروشگاه جدید را تا روز شکرگزاری باز کند - اما تامین کنندگانی که به دلیل ورشکستگی ویرانگر آن در سال 2017 سوخته بودند، همچنان در مورد تجارت با اپراتورهای جدید خرده‌فروش تردید دارند. Go Retail Group - یک فروشگاه مستقر در تگزاس در دو فروشگاه پاپ تایمز که دارای موقعیت مکانی خاص است. و تقویم com shops — از سال 2024 تاکنون 40 فروشگاه Toys "R" Us در تمام طول سال افتتاح کرده است. این فروشگاه ها را تحت مجوز WHP Global، یک شرکت مستقر در نیویورک که دارای 16 برند از جمله Vera Wang، Marc Jacobs، Anne Klein و Land's End است، افتتاح کرده است. اما از آنجایی که Go Retail به دنبال چهار برابر شدن تعداد مکان‌های Toys "R" Us خود برای فصل مهم تعطیلات است، از تولیدکنندگان اسباب‌بازی می‌خواهد شرایط اعتبار تمدید شده را بپردازند - منابع متعددی به The Post گفته‌اند که تا 180 روز پس از تحویل کالا به فروشگاه‌هایش پرداخت کنند. در پاسخ، بسیاری از فروشندگان از فروشندگان عقب‌نشینی کرده‌اند، و برخی از آنها اشاره کرده‌اند که صنعت مالی بین 9 روز تا 90 روز عادی است. جی فورمن، مدیر اجرایی Basic Fun، سازنده کامیون‌های Tonka و Care Bears، می‌گوید: «آنها باید تأمین‌کننده مالی کسب‌وکار باشند، نه فروشندگانشان». ما قبلاً یک بار از آن جاده رفتیم و به شدت سوختیم و دیگر خود را در آن موقعیت قرار نخواهیم داد.»
آلن دورفمن از Super Impulse - که نسخه‌های کوچک و جیبی از اسباب‌بازی‌ها و بازی‌ها از جمله بازی‌های رومیزی مانند Battleship، Connect 4 و Hungry Hungry Hippos را می‌سازد.

news.originalContent:
Kiah Stokes and Veronica Burton shine for Golden State as Angel Reese’s Atlanta team was stifled by a strong defence.

Kiah Stokes and Veronica Burton each scored 13 points to help secure Golden State’s 64-55 victory over Atlanta, putting the Valkyries on the brink of winning the Women’s NBA Finals.

Tiffany Hayes and reserve Cecilia Zandalasini each added 12 points for the Valkyries while Stokes and Burton each pulled down a team-best eight rebounds in Game 5 on Monday.

Golden State seized a 3-2 lead over the Dream in the best-of-seven championship series, which continues on Thursday in Atlanta.

“We’re not done yet. We’ve got one more,” Stokes said. “We need two hoops, 94 feet and each other and that’s all we need.”

The Valkyries, in only their second WNBA campaign, kept Dream star Angel Reese to seven points on 2-of-8 shooting, although she grabbed a game-high 15 rebounds.

Golden State dominated defensively, keeping Atlanta to a season-low in points on 19-of-65 (29 percent) shooting from the floor.

“That has just been our staple all season. We really rely on our defence,” Stokes said.

“They are tough. We have to make sure we’re all doing our part. It’s a team for a reason.”

Stokes had a game-high four blocked shots and has had at least three blocks in every finals game.

Rhyne Howard led Atlanta with 20 points while Jordin Canada added 12.

The Valkyries have been a hit with spectators in the home arena of the NBA Golden State Warriors.

“You all are amazing,” Stokes screamed to a cheering crowd moments after the triumph. “We couldn’t do this without you all.”
news.content:
کیاه استوکس و ورونیکا برتون برای گلدن استیت درخشیدند در حالی که تیم آتلانتای آنجل ریس توسط یک دفاع قوی خفه شد. کیاه استوکس و ورونیکا برتون هر کدام 13 امتیاز به دست آوردند تا پیروزی 64-55 گلدن استیت را بر آتلانتا تضمین کنند و والکیری ها را در آستانه قهرمانی در مسابقات NBA زنان قرار دهند. تیفانی هیز و سیسیلیا زندالاسینی ذخیره هر کدام 12 امتیاز برای والکری ها به دست آوردند در حالی که استوکس و برتون هر کدام هشت ریباند بهترین تیم را در بازی 5 روز دوشنبه به دست آوردند. گلدن استیت در سری مسابقات قهرمانی بهترین های هفتم، 3-2 از رویا جلو افتاد، که در روز پنجشنبه در آتلانتا ادامه دارد. ما به دو حلقه، 94 فوت و همدیگر نیاز داریم و این تمام چیزی است که نیاز داریم.» والکری ها، تنها در دومین کمپین خود در WNBA، ستاره رویا، آنجل ریس را در تیراندازی 2 از 8 به 7 امتیاز رساندند، اگرچه او 15 ریباند به دست آورد. گلدن استیت در تدافع تسلط داشت و آتلانتا را با امتیاز 19 از 65 (29 درصد) به پایین ترین امتیاز فصل نگه داشت. استوکس گفت: "آنها سخت هستند، ما باید مطمئن شویم که همه نقش خود را انجام می دهیم. این یک تیم به دلایلی است.»
استوکس چهار شوت بلاک کرده و حداقل سه بلاک در هر بازی فینال داشته است. راین هاوارد با 20 امتیاز رهبری آتلانتا را به دست آورد در حالی که جردین کانادا 12 امتیاز به دست آورد. والکیری ها در عرصه خانگی NBA گلدن استیت وریرز مورد توجه تماشاگران قرار گرفته اند. استوکس، "همه شما شگفت انگیز هستید."

news.originalContent:
Mbappe appears to say that the funniest internet meme he had seen was of his face photo-shopped onto that of “a Chinese dictator”.

Kylian Mbappe has been dropped by two major brands in China after a video circulated online in which the French football superstar apparently joked about former Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

In China, jokes about Mao, the country’s founding leader who died in 1976, are considered disrespectful and remain a social taboo.

“Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments,” drinks giant Dongpeng said in a statement on Tuesday, adding that “with immediate effect we are terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappe”.

Advertisements showing AI-generated images of the 27-year-old France captain drinking a Dongpeng sports drink were regularly shown in China during this year’s FIFA World Cup.

Mengniu, China’s largest dairy producer, also cut ties with the Real Madrid forward, who until this incident was hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of followers on social media.

Mbappe is fondly nicknamed “Guigui”, the Chinese translation of “turtle”, due to his popularity as a character in a Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles meme.

“With immediate effect our company is terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappe,” Mengniu said in a statement.

“Mengniu firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people,” it added.

The announcements came after a video emerged online with Mbappe saying the funniest internet meme he had seen was of his face digitally altered onto that of “some guy – I think he’s a Chinese dictator”.

This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao, one of several using the footballer’s face and other historical figures.

“Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe” was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo.

One Weibo user said the “extremely serious wrong remarks … crossed the red line. They are completely unacceptable.”

Others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappe’s image from their energy drink bottles.

Dongqiudi, one of China’s biggest online football outlets, said in a statement on Monday evening that Mbappe’s remarks were “offensive to China and the Chinese people” and “have hurt the feelings of Chinese football fans and the Chinese people”.

In September, Mbappe addressed a previous meme depicting him as a military dictator in an interview with French sports newspaper L’Equipe.

“There’s a part of it that’s funny. You can tell that, for some people, it’s all in good fun. But there is another part that’s a bit less funny because of the damage such people have caused throughout history,” he said.

“Being compared to individuals who murder others, or who have brought misery to millions upon millions of people – well, I don’t think I’ve ever done anything like that in my life,” he said.

The furore in China came a day after Mbappe lost out to Harry Kane for the Ballon d’Or, the most prestigious individual award in football.

Global sports stars who have commented on sensitive topics such as Taiwan, Tibet and Hong Kong have previously caused controversy in China and been dumped by sponsors there.

Former NBA player Dwight Howard referred to Taiwan as a country in 2023 as he appeared in a video with the island’s vice president and current President William Lai Ching-te, causing fury on Chinese social media.

Beijing claims Taiwan is its territory and has threatened to use force to take control.

Houston Rockets general manager Daryl Morey posted a tweet in 2019 supporting Hong Kong protests, leading to China suspending sponsorship deals with the NBA and pulling games off Chinese television for a year.
news.content: به نظر می‌رسد امباپه می‌گوید خنده‌دارترین میم اینترنتی که دیده بود، عکسی از چهره‌اش بود که روی چهره «دیکتاتور چینی» عکس‌فروشی شده بود. کیلیان امباپه توسط دو برند بزرگ در چین پس از انتشار ویدیویی در فضای مجازی که در آن فوق ستاره فوتبال فرانسوی ظاهراً درباره رهبر سابق چین، مائو تسه‌تونگ شوخی می‌کرد، کنار گذاشته شد. بی احترامی است و به عنوان یک تابو اجتماعی باقی می ماند. دونگ‌پنگ غول نوشیدنی روز سه‌شنبه در بیانیه‌ای گفت: «شرکت ما قاطعانه با هرگونه رفتاری که احساسات ملی را توهین می‌کند مخالف است و یک سیاست مدارا صفر دارد» و افزود: «با اثر فوری، همه همکاری‌ها را با کیلیان ام‌باپه قطع می‌کنیم». جام جهانی فوتبال سال منگنیو، بزرگترین تولیدکننده لبنیات چین، همچنین روابط خود را با مهاجم رئال مادرید قطع کرد، که تا این اتفاق در میان هواداران چینی با میلیون‌ها دنبال کننده در شبکه‌های اجتماعی محبوبیت زیادی داشت. به دلیل محبوبیت او به عنوان یک شخصیت در لاک‌پشت‌های نینجا نوجوان، لقب «گوئی‌گی» (Guigui)، ترجمه‌ی چینی «لاک‌پشت» به امباپه داده می‌شود. منگنیو در بیانیه‌ای گفت: «شرکت ما بلافاصله همکاری خود را با کیلیان امباپه قطع می‌کند.» منگنیو قاطعانه مخالفت می‌کند و در قبال هر حرف یا عملی که به احساسات مردم چین آسیب می‌زند، سیاست مدارا صفر دارد.

news.originalContent:
Exit polls are expected soon after voting closes late on Tuesday, but a final verdict might take days.

Israelis are voting in a closely watched election to decide on the direction of the country, three years after the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack on southern Israel that set off the genocidal war on Gaza.

The first election since those attacks comes at a time when Israel’s pogroms in the occupied West Bank have escalated, and amid mounting tensions with several of its neighbours, many of whom it has attacked in the past three years.

But the vote also comes amid growing domestic questions that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces over alleged failures that allowed the October 7 attack, his government’s handling of efforts to retrieve captives taken to Gaza, alleged corruption and disputes over ultra-Orthodox military service.

In final polls published Friday, Netanyahu’s coalition is expected to be neck and neck with – or trail slightly behind – the opposition bloc led by former Israeli military chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot.

According to Israeli news outlet Haaretz, which has collated polls from Israeli news channels, as of Friday, an average of Channels 11, 12 and 13 predicts Netanyahu’s bloc will win 50 seats while Eisenkot’s opposition bloc will take 54 seats. The Israeli parliament, known as the Knesset, has 120 seats in all, so 61 is the mark that a grouping needs to reach a majority.

Here’s what you need to know about the election.

On Tuesday, polls opened at 7am local time (05:00 GMT) and will end at 10pm (20:00 GMT).

About 7.3 million Israelis will be eligible to vote, including 1.2 million Palestinian citizens of Israel. Israelis living abroad cannot vote because the country does not have a general absentee ballot, requiring voters to be physically present on election day.

Diplomats and state emissaries are the exception and cast their ballots at Israeli missions on October 20.

News channels will broadcast exit poll results once the election ends, with the first indications likely within a few hours of polls closing, but it could take days or weeks to get a clear result.

Results will also be live on the Central Elections Committee website once polls close.

While a clear picture of the election results may come out quickly, if no party or coalition secures a majority, it could take much longer.

The final vote tally is expected by Friday, and official election results are formally published a week after the election, on November 4.

Under a proportional representation system, Israelis vote for a single party, not individual candidates.

The number of seats the party gains in the Knesset is linked to the proportion of the vote it receives. For example, if Netanyahu’s Likud party secures 50 percent of the national vote, it would take 50 percent of the Knesset’s 120 seats.

A majority requires 61 of the 120 seats.

For a party to enter the Knesset, it must secure at least 3.25 percent of the national vote.

About a dozen parties are widely thought to have a chance of crossing the threshold, so the final tally and seat allocation will take time.

Once the final count is in, President Isaac Herzog will speak with party leaders about who they want as prime minister, then tap the candidate he believes has the best chance of forming a government.

The person nominated then has up to 42 days to form a government. As it stands, no single party in Israel has ever won an outright majority, so governments are formed by a coalition of parties, and negotiations on forming a government often take weeks.

If no government emerges, the current cabinet, Netanyahu’s government, will remain as a caretaker government.

But before that point, whoever gains the most votes will have different options to assemble support from smaller parties, including forming a minority government or working with another political leader to alternate as prime minister under a power-sharing arrangement.

If all negotiations fail, and no grouping is able to cobble together a workable government, new elections will have to be called.
news.content: انتظار می‌رود که نظرسنجی‌های خروج به زودی پس از پایان رای‌گیری در اواخر روز سه‌شنبه، اما صدور حکم نهایی ممکن است چند روز طول بکشد. سه سال پس از حمله حماس به جنوب اسرائیل که آغازگر جنگ نسل‌کشی در غزه بود، در یک انتخابات تحت نظارت دقیق برای تصمیم‌گیری در مورد مسیر کشور رای می‌دهند. اولین انتخابات پس از آن حملات در زمانی برگزار می شود که قتل عام اسرائیل در کرانه باختری اشغالی تشدید شده است، و در بحبوحه تنش های فزاینده با چندین همسایه خود، که به بسیاری از آنها در سه سال گذشته حمله کرده است. اما این رای همچنین در بحبوحه سوالات داخلی فزاینده ای است که بنیامین نتانیاهو، نخست وزیر، در مورد شکست های ادعایی که باعث حمله 7 اکتبر شد، نحوه مدیریت تلاش های دولت او برای بازگرداندن اسیران به غزه، فساد ادعایی و اختلافات بر سر خدمات نظامی افراطی ارتدوکس، با آن مواجه است. در نظرسنجی‌های نهایی منتشر شده در روز جمعه، انتظار می‌رود ائتلاف نتانیاهو با بلوک اپوزیسیون به رهبری گادی آیزنکوت، رئیس سابق ستاد ارتش اسرائیل، همسایه باشد - یا کمی عقب‌تر باشد. بر اساس گزارش خبرگزاری اسرائیلی هاآرتص، که نظرسنجی‌های کانال‌های خبری اسرائیل را جمع‌آوری کرده است، تا روز جمعه، به‌طور میانگین از شبکه‌های خبری اسراییلی 1113 Channelslocya و Ne11. 50 کرسی به دست خواهد آورد در حالی که بلوک مخالف آیزنکوت 54 کرسی را به دست خواهد آورد. پارلمان اسرائیل، معروف به کنست، در مجموع 120 کرسی دارد، بنابراین 61 کرسی علامتی است که یک گروه برای دستیابی به اکثریت نیاز دارد. در اینجا آنچه باید در مورد انتخابات بدانید، آمده است. روز سه شنبه، رای گیری در ساعت 7 صبح باز شد.

news.originalContent:
British-Iranian dual national Mohmed Abdulkarim and British citizen Nouman Essghir charged under the National Security Act.

British prosecutors say they ⁠⁠have charged two men with ‌‌offences under the National Security Act following an incident ⁠⁠in September ⁠⁠at RAF Fairford, an ⁠⁠airbase in England used ⁠⁠by ⁠⁠the United States.

British-Iranian dual national Mohmed Abdulkarim and British citizen Nouman Essghir, both aged 24, were charged under the National Security Act, the Crown Prosecution Service said. They are due to appear in court later on Tuesday.

Abdulkarim is charged with assisting Iran’s intelligence service, and Essghir with entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the United Kingdom.

The airbase in Gloucestershire, southwestern England, had been used by US bombers to carry out strikes on Iran this year.

Essghir was arrested outside the base on September 27, when armed police officers and army bomb-disposal experts swarmed the rural area. Dozens of residents were evacuated from their homes as police and army bomb-disposal experts searched for explosives.

Abdulkarim was arrested in the past week. Six other men have been arrested and released on bail as investigations continue.

Shortly after the incident at the base, US B-1 bombers were withdrawn from the site.

Assistant Commissioner Laurence ‌Taylor, head of the UK Counter Terrorism Policing, said police believed ‌the country ‌Abdulkarim was assisting was Iran.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham last week said the activity at RAF Fairford was likely to have been coordinated in Iran, which Iran’s ambassador to the UK has denied.

Last year the UK said there had been 20 credible Iranian-backed threats to kill or kidnap individuals based in the UK.

In July, Britain used new powers to ban support for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and a linked group, Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya (HAYI), which had claimed responsibility for seven attacks earlier this year at locations linked to Jewish and Israeli communities, and Persian-language media.
news.content: محمد عبدالکریم دو تابعیتی ایرانی-بریتانیایی و نعمان اسغیر شهروند بریتانیایی بر اساس قانون امنیت ملی متهم شدند. دادستان های بریتانیا می گویند که دو مرد را به ارتکاب جرایم بر اساس قانون امنیت ملی پس از حادثه ای در سپتامبر در RAF Fairford، یک پایگاه مورد استفاده در انگلستان متهم کرده اند. ایالات متحده آمریکا. سرویس دادستانی ولیعهد عربستان گفت که محمد عبدالکریم دو تابعیتی انگلیسی-ایرانی و نعمان اسغیر شهروند بریتانیایی که هر دو 24 ساله هستند، بر اساس قانون امنیت ملی متهم شدند. آنها قرار است بعداً روز سه‌شنبه در دادگاه حاضر شوند. عبدالکریم به کمک به سرویس اطلاعاتی ایران و اسغیر به ورود به مکان ممنوعه برای اهدافی که برای بریتانیا ضرر دارد متهم است. پایگاه هوایی در گلوسسترشر، جنوب غربی انگلستان، توسط بمب افکن های آمریکایی برای انجام حملات علیه ایران در سال جاری مورد استفاده قرار گرفته بود. اسغیر در خارج از پایگاه در 27 سپتامبر دستگیر شد، زمانی که افسران پلیس مسلح و کارشناسان خنثی سازی بمب ارتش به منطقه روستایی هجوم آوردند. در حالی که پلیس و کارشناسان خنثی سازی بمب ارتش در جستجوی مواد منفجره بودند، ده ها تن از ساکنان از خانه های خود تخلیه شدند. عبدالکریم در هفته گذشته دستگیر شد. با ادامه تحقیقات، شش مرد دیگر دستگیر و به قید وثیقه آزاد شدند. اندکی پس از حادثه در پایگاه، بمب‌افکن‌های B-1 آمریکا از محل خارج شدند. لورنس تیلور، معاون کمیسر، رئیس پلیس ضد تروریسم بریتانیا، گفت که پلیس معتقد است که عبدالکریم به نخست‌وزیر این کشور کمک می‌کند و بریتیش ایران است.
